title: Cross-zone evacuation policy and retention-proofing for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Problem statement: For Private/VPC/on-prem customers we must guarantee that automated regional failover and maintenance operations never violate contractual data residency constraints and that every movement or deletion of data is accompanied by tamper-evident evidence suitable for audits. Current behavior allows emergency evacuations to route traffic to nearest healthy region which can cross legal boundaries (e.g., EU -> US) under severe load. We need a controlled policy and implementation that: 

1) Enforces residency boundary checks at the routing layer (no automatic cross-jurisdiction failover without explicit policy and approvals).
2) Provides configurable retention and purge lifecycle for ephemeral artifacts (KV caches, prefix caches, logs) and long-term persisted evidence.
3) Produces cryptographically-signed evidence bundles for any evacuation, retention change, or cross-region transfer that are stored in a compliant evidence store and surfaced to customers and compliance teams.

Scope: Platform-side controls for Private and VPC deployments (not hosted-API fallbacks). Covers routing policy enforcement, evacuation windows, emergency approval workflow, retention lifecycle enforcement for both cached and persisted artifacts, evidence generation pipeline, console + API UX for policy configuration, and audit report automation. Exclusions: on-prem hardware orchestration (customer-managed) beyond advisory playbooks; we will provide operators with tooling and signed manifests but not force on-prem network actions.
acceptance_criteria: No automated failover across configured data-residency boundaries unless explicit per-customer policy allows it
Evacuation request flow includes justification, TTL, and an approver role when crossing jurisdictional boundaries
Retention settings configurable per-customer and per-artifact type (KV-cache, prefix cache, request logs, persisted models) and enforced by GC and retention daemon
Evidence bundles produced for every evacuation or cross-region transfer: signed manifest, hash list, timestamp, actor id, and retention action recorded
Evidence bundles are immutable, stored in the customer’s approved evidence store (S3-like with region tag or on-prem equivalent) and indexed in the Console audit view
Automated daily compliance report for active Private deployments delivered to compliance S3 path and Slack channel; ad-hoc report API available
End-to-end tests and a canary run performed against a sandbox Private deployment without violating simulated residency constraints
implementation_steps: Design routing-layer residency check and policy model (policy schema + precedence rules)
Add evacuation API endpoint: POST /v1/private/{tenant}/evacuation with justification, desired failover region, and approver list
Integrate an approval workflow backed by RBAC and audit logs (Console + API triggers)
Implement retention daemon to enforce per-artifact TTLs with safe-delete windows and signed deletion manifests
Build evidence bundle generator (manifest, SHA256 list, signer via KMS/HSM, metadata) and immutable storage interface
Expose evidence and retention state in Console UI and provide report/export endpoints
Add end-to-end integration tests and fuzz tests for policy precedence and edge cases
Author runbook and customer-facing advisory for emergency evacuations on on-prem deployments
